top_choice_rationale: P001 awards Katori and Ye for optical lattice clocks. The magic-wavelength condition is a distinct principle: it cancels the trap light shift so that many neutral atoms sit in the Lamb-Dicke regime, and it has been reproduced in Sr, Yb and Hg across independent laboratories at the 1e-18 level, which settles maturity. The two-name allocation ties the concept (Katori) and the record-setting realisation (Ye) to one citation, and the wording confines Ye's credit to the lattice clock and claims nothing on combs, nuclear clocks or the redefinition of the second. The open priority questions (Takamoto, Ido, Lemonde) are real but sit at the edges of the credit, so awarding is preferable to no award.
